links.outcome: Public reporting of sex- and age-specific data in clinical studies of FDA-approved AI devices
links.effect: Among clinical studies, 145 (28.7%) provided sex-specific data and 117 (23.2%) addressed age-related subgroups.
links.quote: Among clinical studies, less than one-third provided sex-specific data (145 studies [28.7%]), and only 117 studies (23.2%) addressed age-related subgroups.

links.outcome: Reporting of discriminatory performance metrics in public summaries
links.effect: Reported in 200 summaries; sensitivity 183 devices (36.2%), specificity 176 (34.9%), AUC 82 (16.2%).
links.quote: Discriminatory performance metrics were reported in 200 of the available summaries (sensitivity: 183 devices [36.2%]; specificity: 176 devices [34.9%]; area under the curve: 82 devices [16.2%]).

links.outcome: Study designs of clinical performance studies for approved AI devices
links.effect: Retrospective 193 (38.2%); prospective 41 (8.1%); randomized 12 (2.4%). 218 devices (24.1%) reported no performance studies.
links.quote: Retrospective study designs were most common (193 studies [38.2%]), with only 41 studies (8.1%) being prospective and 12 studies (2.4%) randomized.

links.outcome: Availability of development details in publicly provided device summaries
links.effect: Detailed descriptions of development were absent from most publicly provided summaries.
links.quote: Detailed descriptions of development were absent from most publicly provided summaries.

screen.reason: Cross-sectional meta-research study evaluating the public evidence and validation characteristics (clinical generalizability metrics, subgroup reporting) supporting 903 FDA-approved AI medical devices.
